headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because aci has broad network egress and CRM/email access while ai-engineering-hub is non-egress and undocumented for verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use direct function calls or MCP and touches email/CRM data, so if ai-engineering-hub content is bridged into aci via shared files or copied prompts, instruction hijacking is plausible. ai-engineering-hub has no io_surfaces, so the interaction is inferred rather than documented; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange text through a shared file, clipboard, or MCP message channel
IF ai-engineering-hub content is rendered as instructions inside aci's prompt or tool context
mitigations: Disable any shared clipboard or shared workspace between the agents
Prefix all imported text with a non-executable delimiter and provenance label
Require manual review before aci acts on ai-engineering-hub output
Use separate MCP servers or disable MCP bridging
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware prompt filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci has broad network egress and handles email, CRM, and support data, while ai-engineering-hub has no egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive aci data could be exposed through copied context or uploads. The pairwise leak path is not directly documented, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or files
IF aci forwards file contents or context into external APIs
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials for each agent
Remove sensitive files from any shared directory
Turn off automatic file attachment or context upload in aci
Review outbound API destinations before running the pair
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and can write through APIs, but ai-engineering-hub is not runnable and shows no write surfaces. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; only unusual shared-resource setups would create contention.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource
IF ai-engineering-hub is wrapped in a separate runtime that gains write access
mitigations: Avoid pointing both agents at the same CRM or document store
Serialize any shared updates through one operator
Use separate API credentials per agent
Check for duplicate writes in logs after a test run

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM, email, and calendar actions, and ai-engineering-hub is a non-runnable docs repo with no verification surface. If aci's output is fed into downstream automation without a human check, errors can cascade into real actions. The lack of documented validation between them warrants medium.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub output is used as authoritative input to aci
IF aci is allowed to send email, update CRM, or schedule calendar events without review
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before any outbound action
Require source citations for any factual claim before execution
Run a dry-run mode for one cycle and inspect outputs
Limit aci to read-only operations until validated
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before action

E_compliance.rationale: aci touches customer support, email, CRM, and calendar data, which can carry regulated personal data, while ai-engineering-hub has no stated residency or retention controls. Because the pair lacks documented compliance alignment, the safest reading is a policy mismatch risk rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is processed through aci
IF ai-engineering-hub artifacts are retained or logged alongside that data
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before sharing records
Keep regulated data out of any shared prompts or files
Set short retention on logs and exports
Document residency and retention expectations for both tools
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
